finding.sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: control login with HS256-signed JWT succeeds; attack login with alg=none but same semantic claims should be rejected (proof integrity).
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted an unsigned JWT (alg=none) for JWT auth login; authenticity was not enforced on the consumed proof

sequence.description: Direct JWT endpoint: control login with HS256-signed JWT succeeds; attack login with alg=none but same semantic claims should be rejected (proof integrity).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: Vault must not accept an unsigned JWT (alg=none) even if the semantic claims (sub/aud/iss) match a valid token; verification must apply to the exact consumed proof.

params.description: jwt mount for I1 alg=none test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control JWT login/read failed; cannot interpret alg=none rejection as proof-integrity enforcement
Vault accepted an unsigned JWT (alg=none) for JWT auth login; authenticity was not enforced on the consumed proof

finding.sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: rotate trust anchor from legitimate key to attacker key and verify old-key tokens are rejected immediately; tests that verification policy actually applies to consumed proof after config change.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_legit_after_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_legit_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault continued accepting JWTs that only validate under the previous trust anchor after reconfiguration; verification policy may not be applied to the consumed proof

sequence.description: Direct JWT endpoint: rotate trust anchor from legitimate key to attacker key and verify old-key tokens are rejected immediately; tests that verification policy actually applies to consumed proof after config change.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: After an admin trust-anchor change, Vault must verify JWT signatures against the currently configured trust source; it must not accept tokens whose signature only validates under a previous trust anchor.

params.description: jwt mount for I1 trust-anchor substitution test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline login with initial trust anchor failed; cannot interpret post-rotation behavior
Vault continued accepting JWTs that only validate under the previous trust anchor after reconfiguration; verification policy may not be applied to the consumed proof
Post-rotation login with the newly configured trust anchor failed; cannot distinguish enforcement from misconfiguration

finding.sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt kid-injection by signing with an attacker key and setting kid to a plausible value; Vault must reject because the key is not in the configured trust source.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_kid_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_kid_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted attacker-signed JWT by trusting attacker-controlled kid/header rather than configured trust anchor.

sequence.description: Direct JWT login: attempt kid-injection by signing with an attacker key and setting kid to a plausible value; Vault must reject because the key is not in the configured trust source.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: Vault must verify the JWT signature against the configured trust anchor; attacker-signed JWTs must not be accepted even if kid/header values are manipulated to look legitimate.

params.description: jwt auth for I1 kid injection test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control JWT login/read failed; cannot interpret kid-injection rejection as proof-integrity enforcement.
Vault accepted attacker-signed JWT by trusting attacker-controlled kid/header rather than configured trust anchor.

finding.sequence_description: I1 attack: attempt JWKS kid-collision / cache-poisoning by reconfiguring jwks_url to attacker-controlled keys that reuse the same kid as the legitimate key, then re-auth with the same semantic JWT claims. Vault must apply the updated verification policy to the consumed proof and reject tokens signed by the old key after rotation.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_legit_jwks_read_status == 200
Evaluation: user_legit_jwks_read_status=403 == 200 → False
Implication: Control flow failed: legitimate JWT under legitimate JWKS could not read the protected secret (setup/trust source may be broken).

sequence.description: I1 attack: attempt JWKS kid-collision / cache-poisoning by reconfiguring jwks_url to attacker-controlled keys that reuse the same kid as the legitimate key, then re-auth with the same semantic JWT claims. Vault must apply the updated verification policy to the consumed proof and reject tokens signed by the old key after rotation.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: After a trust-source change, Vault must verify the exact JWT proof against the currently configured JWKS (including correct key selection by kid) and must not accept a JWT whose signature only validates under the prior JWKS or a stale cached key.

params.description: jwt mount for I1 kid-collision cache-poison test

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control flow failed: legitimate JWT under legitimate JWKS could not read the protected secret (setup/trust source may be broken).
Vault accepted a JWT signed by the old key after JWKS trust source was rotated, suggesting stale verification policy or cached key selection (kid collision/cache-poison risk).
Attacker obtained read access to protected secret after swapping JWKS to attacker-controlled keys with the same kid, indicating proof integrity failure in key selection/verification binding.

finding.sequence_description: I2 attack: Demonstrate that a token with nbf slightly in the future is rejected under strict leeway, then loosen leeway via role config change and re-auth to ensure acceptance only occurs when policy allows (no stale acceptance under strict policy).
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nbf_after_loosen_login_status == 200
Evaluation: user_attacker_nbf_after_loosen_login_status=400 == 200 → False
Implication: After loosening leeway, token still rejected; indicates config change not applied to new logins (stale policy application)

sequence.description: I2 attack: Demonstrate that a token with nbf slightly in the future is rejected under strict leeway, then loosen leeway via role config change and re-auth to ensure acceptance only occurs when policy allows (no stale acceptance under strict policy).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I2: Tokens must not be accepted before their nbf time when leeway is disabled; after tightening/loosening time-leeway config, new logins must reflect the current policy (no unintended reuse/acceptance under the old stricter policy).

params.description: jwt mount for nbf/leeway reauth tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed; cannot interpret nbf enforcement
Token with nbf far in the future was accepted even with not_before_leeway disabled
After loosening leeway, token still rejected; indicates config change not applied to new logins (stale policy application)

finding.sequence_description: I5 attack: Use claim_mappings to map an untrusted claim into a privileged policy name; verify Vault does not grant unintended policies.
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_mapping_user_read_status == 200
Evaluation: user_victim_mapping_user_read_status=403 == 200 → False
Implication: Control user could not read user path; test setup invalid or role/policy misconfigured.

sequence.description: I5 attack: Use claim_mappings to map an untrusted claim into a privileged policy name; verify Vault does not grant unintended policies.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed BrokerPolicy(config); untrusted JWT claims must not be able to inject/override granted_policies via claim_mappings.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker injected requested_policy=admin-secrets via claim_mappings and gained admin secret read; effective permissions exceeded broker policy.

oracle_checks.assertion: "admin-secrets" not in user_attacker_mapping_policies AND "admin-secrets" not in user_attacker_mapping_identity_policies
oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker token included admin-secrets policy due to claim mapping injection.
Control user could not read user path; test setup invalid or role/policy misconfigured.
